records.source: לְדָוִ֡דאֵלֶ֥יךָ יְ֝הוָ֗ה נַפְשִׁ֥י אֶשָּֽׂא׃
records.gloss: Of David. To you, YHWH, my soul I lift up.
pieces: Of David. To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I lift up my whole self.

L.1: Of David. To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I lift up my soul.

R.1: By David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I turn my whole heart to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and pray.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: Psalm 25: an alphabet poem
decisions.reason: The psalm is an acrostic: its verses begin with the letters of the Hebrew alphabet in order, one letter to a verse. The pattern is not exact: one or two letters are missing or repeated, and a last verse beginning with the letter pe (verse 22) stands outside the alphabet, as the last verse of Psalm 34 does.

decisions.choice: I lift up my soul: I long for you, I pray to you
decisions.reason: To lift up the soul to someone is to set one's desire and hope on them (86:4; 143:8); the word for soul (nefesh) also means desire. The psalm opens as a prayer of trust.

decisions.choice: my whole self
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "soul" means here, the whole person (m3).

decisions.choice: I turn my whole heart to you and pray
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m3).

records.heading: Teach me your paths and forgive me

records.source: אֱֽלֹהַ֗י בְּךָ֣ בָ֭טַחְתִּי אַל־אֵב֑וֹשָׁה אַל־יַֽעַלְצ֖וּ אֹיְבַ֣י לִֽי׃
records.gloss: My God, in you I trust; let me not be put to shame; let not my enemies exult over me.
pieces: My God, I trust in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; do not let me be disgraced, and do not let my enemies gloat over me.

L.2: My God, in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I trust; let me not be put to shame; let not my enemies exult over me.

R.2: My God, I trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Do not let me end up ashamed. Do not let my enemies laugh at me and celebrate.

decisions.choice: be put to shame: be let down, disgraced
decisions.reason: The verb (bosh) is the shame of a hope that fails: the one who trusted is shown up as a fool before others. The psalm asks three times that this not happen (verses 2, 3, 20).

decisions.choice: My God: the alphabet pattern bends
decisions.reason: The verse should begin with the second letter of the alphabet (bet). It begins with "My God", and the bet word ("in you") comes next; the address to God may have been placed in front.

decisions.choice: exult over me: gloat in triumph
decisions.reason: The verb ('alats) is open rejoicing; over a fallen enemy it is gloating.

records.source: גַּ֣ם כָּל־קֹ֭וֶיךָ לֹ֣א יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ יֵ֝בֹ֗שׁוּ הַבּוֹגְדִ֥ים רֵיקָֽם׃
records.gloss: Indeed all who wait for you will not be put to shame; they will be put to shame, those acting treacherously without cause.
pieces: Indeed, everyone who waits for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be spared disgrace; it is those who betray others for nothing who will be disgraced.

L.3: Indeed, none who wait for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be put to shame; they will be put to shame who act treacherously without cause.

R.3: People who wait for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to act will never be let down. But people who are disloyal for no reason will be put to shame.

decisions.choice: wait for: hope in, look to with expectation
decisions.reason: To wait (qavah) for God is to look to him with hope and keep expecting him to act (27:14; Isaiah 40:31). The word returns in verses 5 and 21.

decisions.choice: act treacherously without cause: betray for no reason
decisions.reason: The verb (bagad) is breaking faith with someone one is bound to; "without cause" (reqam) means for nothing, with no wrong done to them.

decisions.choice: will not be put to shame: a confident statement
alternatives: let none ... be put to shame (a wish)
decisions.reason: The verbs can be read as a statement or as a wish; read as a statement, the verse gives the ground for the prayer of verse 2.

records.source: דְּרָכֶ֣יךָ יְ֭הוָה הוֹדִיעֵ֑נִי אֹ֖רְחוֹתֶ֣יךָלַמְּדֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Your ways, YHWH, make me know; your paths teach me.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, let me come to know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways; teach me to follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} paths.

L.4: Your ways, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, make known to me; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} paths teach me.

R.4: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show me how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want me to live. Teach me which road to take.

decisions.choice: your ways, your paths: the life you approve
decisions.reason: God's ways and paths are the way of life he shows and wants people to walk in (Exodus 33:13; Psalm 27:11). The prayer is to be taught to live by them.

decisions.choice: to follow (B); which road to take (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the teaching is for walking in these paths (m1).

records.source: הַדְרִ֘יכֵ֤נִי בַאֲמִתֶּ֨ךָ׀וְֽלַמְּדֵ֗נִי כִּֽי־אַ֭תָּה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעִ֑י אוֹתְךָ֥ קִ֝וִּ֗יתִי כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Lead me in your truth and teach me, for you [are the] God of my salvation; for you I have waited all the day.
pieces: Lead me by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness and teach me, since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the God who saves me; it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I wait for the whole day through.

L.5: Lead me in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth and teach me, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are the] God of my salvation; for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have waited all the day.

R.5: Help me live by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth, and teach me. You are my God, the one who saves me. I keep waiting for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all day.

decisions.choice: your truth: your faithfulness, your reliable word
decisions.reason: The word ('emet) means what is firm and reliable: God's truth and his faithfulness are one. To be led in it is to live by what God has shown to be true and to rely on him to keep faith (verse 10; 26:3).

decisions.choice: God of my salvation: the God who saves me
decisions.reason: The phrase names God by what he does for the psalmist: he rescues him (27:9).

decisions.choice: for you I have waited: you, and no one else
decisions.reason: The object comes first for emphasis: the psalmist's hope is in God alone.

decisions.choice: the God who saves me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means (m2).

records.source: זְכֹר־רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ יְ֭הוָה וַחֲסָדֶ֑יךָ כִּ֖י מֵעוֹלָ֣ם הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: Remember your compassions, YHWH, and your loyal loves, for from of old they [are].
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, keep in mind {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tender mercies and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} acts of loyal love; they have been {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} since ancient times.

L.6: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, for they [are] from of old.

R.6: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember how kind and full of faithful love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have always been. You have been that way from the very beginning.

decisions.choice: compassion: tender, motherly mercy
decisions.reason: The word (rachamim) is related to the word for womb: the love of a parent for a child (103:13; Isaiah 49:15). It is plural here, for its many acts.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps its commitments, the faithful kindness of the covenant (Exodus 34:6-7). It is plural here: the many times God has shown it.

decisions.choice: Remember: act on what you know
decisions.reason: When God remembers, he acts on what he remembers (Genesis 8:1). The next verse turns the word around: do not remember my sins, but remember me.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: Readable's usual wording for chesed (m2).

records.source: חַטֹּ֤אות נְעוּרַ֨י׀וּפְשָׁעַ֗י אַל־תִּ֫זְכֹּ֥ר כְּחַסְדְּךָ֥ זְכָר־לִי־אַ֑תָּה לְמַ֖עַן טוּבְךָ֣ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] sins of my youth and my transgressions do not remember; according to your loyal love remember me, you, for the sake of your goodness, YHWH.
pieces: Do not hold against me the sins of my youth or my acts of rebellion; in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love remember me, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.7: The sins of my youth and my transgressions do not remember; according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love remember me — {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} — for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: Do not keep thinking about the wrong things I did when I was young, or the times I turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Think of me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are good, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: transgressions: acts of rebellion
decisions.reason: The word (pesha') is a breaking away from a lord, rebellion against God, not only missing the mark (chatta't, "sins").

decisions.choice: do not remember: do not hold against me
decisions.reason: For God not to remember sins is to forgive them and not act on them (Isaiah 43:25; Jeremiah 31:34).

decisions.choice: you: emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is added for emphasis: whatever others may do, you remember me.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps its commitments, the faithful kindness of the covenant (Exodus 34:6-7).

decisions.choice: Do not hold against me
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the idiom means (m2).

decisions.choice: the times I turned against you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word means and whom the rebellion was against (m1).

records.source: טוֹב־וְיָשָׁ֥ר יְהוָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֤ן יוֹרֶ֖ה חַטָּאִ֣ים בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: Good and upright [is] YHWH; therefore he teaches sinners in the way.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good and upright; that is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows sinners the way to go.

L.8: Good and upright [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; therefore {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructs sinners in the way.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good and always does what is right. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows sinners the right way to live.

decisions.choice: instructs: teaches, points the way
decisions.reason: The verb (yarah) means to point or direct; the word torah, instruction, comes from it. God's goodness shows itself in teaching even sinners.

decisions.choice: the LORD: the prayer turns to speak about God
decisions.reason: From here to verse 15 the psalm speaks about the LORD, before it turns back to prayer in verse 16.

records.source: יַדְרֵ֣ךְ עֲ֭נָוִים בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וִֽילַמֵּ֖ד עֲנָוִ֣ים דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: He leads humble [ones] in the justice, and he teaches humble [ones] his way.
pieces: He directs the lowly in what is just, and to the lowly {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} teaches {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way.

L.9: He leads [the] humble in what is right, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} teaches [the] humble {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way.

R.9: He shows humble people how to do what is right. He teaches them how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants them to live.

decisions.choice: the humble: the lowly who depend on God
decisions.reason: The word ('anavim) is used of the poor and the humble, people who have no power of their own and look to God (9:19; 10:17). It is repeated for emphasis.

decisions.choice: what is right: justice
decisions.reason: The word (mishpat) is justice, the right way of acting.

records.source: כָּל־אָרְח֣וֹת יְ֭הוָה חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֑ת לְנֹצְרֵ֥י בְ֝רִית֗וֹ וְעֵדֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: All [the] paths of YHWH [are] loyal love and faithfulness for keepers of his covenant and his testimonies.
pieces: Every path {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes is loyal love and faithfulness toward all who hold to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees.

L.10: All the paths of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] loyal love and faithfulness for those who keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} always acts with faithful love and keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word to people who keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps its commitments. Paired with faithfulness ('emet), it echoes the LORD's own description of himself in Exodus 34:6.

decisions.choice: testimonies: the terms of the covenant
decisions.reason: The word ('edot) is the covenant's written terms, which bear witness to what God requires (19:8; Deuteronomy 4:45).

decisions.choice: the paths of the LORD: the way God deals with people
decisions.reason: Here God's paths are his own ways of acting toward those who keep his covenant.

decisions.choice: always acts with faithful love and keeps his word
alternatives: all the paths of the LORD are loyal love and faithfulness
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of paths means (m3), and says "keeps his word" for faithfulness.

records.source: לְמַֽעַן־שִׁמְךָ֥ יְהוָ֑ה וְֽסָלַחְתָּ֥ לַ֝עֲוֺנִ֗י כִּ֣י רַב־הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: For the sake of your name, YHWH, and you will forgive my iniquity, for great [is] it.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, forgive the wrong I have done, because it is so great.

L.11: For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, forgive my iniquity, for it [is] great.

R.11: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, forgive my sin, because it is very great. Do it to show what kind of God {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your name: for your own honor
decisions.reason: God's name is his character as he has made it known; to act for its sake is to act true to himself (23:3; Ezekiel 36:22).

decisions.choice: forgive: a request
decisions.reason: The verb form, joined by "and", carries on the plea of the verses before.

decisions.choice: for it is great: the reason for the plea
decisions.reason: The word ki usually gives a reason: the guilt is too great for anyone but God to deal with. Some read it as "though".

decisions.choice: Do it to show what kind of God you are
alternatives: for the sake of your name
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m1).

records.source: מִי־זֶ֣ה הָ֭אִישׁ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה י֝וֹרֶ֗נּוּ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יִבְחָֽר׃
records.gloss: Who [is] this, the man fearing YHWH? He will teach him in [the] way he will choose.
pieces: Is there anyone who fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? He will show that person which way to choose.

L.12: Who [is] {{gender:the person|the man}} who fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? He will instruct {{gender:them|him}} in the way {{gender:they|he}} should choose.

R.12: What about people who respect {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? He will teach them the right path to choose.

decisions.choice: fears the LORD: honors him with reverence and obeys him
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to take him seriously, honoring and obeying him (111:10; Proverbs 1:7). It is not terror.

decisions.choice: he should choose: the person chooses the way
decisions.reason: "He will choose" may refer to the person, who is taught which way to choose, or to God, who teaches the way he himself has chosen.

decisions.choice: the man: anyone who fears the LORD
decisions.reason: The word (ha'ish) is a type of person, as in 1:1; anyone who fears the LORD.

decisions.choice: the person, them, they; with "the man", "him", "he" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The person is anyone who fears the LORD (m3).

records.source: נַ֭פְשׁוֹ בְּט֣וֹב תָּלִ֑ין וְ֝זַרְע֗וֹ יִ֣ירַשׁ אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: His soul in good will lodge, and his offspring will possess [the] land.
pieces: They will live their lives in well-being, and their descendants will possess the land.

L.13: {{gender:Their|His}} soul will lodge in good, and {{gender:their|his}} offspring will possess [the] land.

R.13: They will have good lives, and their children will own the land after them.

decisions.choice: his soul will lodge in good: he will live in well-being
decisions.reason: The verb (lin) means to spend the night, to stay; the person will rest in what is good, in plenty and peace.

decisions.choice: will possess the land: the promise to the faithful
decisions.reason: The land was promised to Abraham's offspring (Genesis 15:7); Psalm 37 repeats that the humble and righteous will possess it (37:9, 11, 29).

decisions.choice: they, their
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the person of verse 12 as "he"; Balanced and Readable use the plural, which includes men and women alike.

decisions.choice: their, with "his" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

records.source: ס֣וֹד יְ֭הוָה לִירֵאָ֑יו וּ֝בְרִית֗וֹ לְהוֹדִיעָֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] counsel of YHWH [is] for those fearing him, and his covenant, to make them know.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} takes those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} confidence; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lets them know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant.

L.14: The counsel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] for those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, to make [it] known to them.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is a close friend to people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He shows them what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant means.

decisions.choice: counsel: close friendship, confidence
decisions.reason: The word (sod) is the circle of close friends who share their plans, and so friendship and confidences (Job 29:4; Proverbs 3:32). God shares his mind with those who fear him.

decisions.choice: his covenant, to make it known: he lets them know it
decisions.reason: The second half is short: "and his covenant, to make them know", meaning he makes his covenant known to them.

decisions.choice: is a close friend to
alternatives: the counsel of the LORD is for
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word means (m1).

records.source: עֵינַ֣י תָּ֭מִיד אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י הֽוּא־יוֹצִ֖יא מֵרֶ֣שֶׁת רַגְלָֽי׃
records.gloss: My eyes [are] always toward YHWH, for he will bring out from [the] net my feet.
pieces: I never stop looking to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pull my feet free of the net.

L.15: My eyes [are] always toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring my feet out of the net.

R.15: I always look to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. He will set me free from the traps my enemies set for me.

decisions.choice: my eyes are toward the LORD: I look to him for help
decisions.reason: Eyes turned to someone show dependence and expectation (123:2; 141:8).

decisions.choice: the net: a hunter's trap
decisions.reason: Birds and animals were caught in nets spread on the ground; enemies' plots are pictured this way (9:16; 31:5).

decisions.choice: he: he and no other
decisions.reason: The pronoun is added for emphasis.

decisions.choice: the traps my enemies set for me
decisions.reason: Readable says who sets the net (m2); the enemies are named in verse 19.

records.source: פְּנֵה־אֵלַ֥י וְחָנֵּ֑נִי כִּֽי־יָחִ֖יד וְעָנִ֣י אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Turn to me and be gracious to me, for alone and afflicted [am] I.
pieces: Turn toward me and show me grace, for I am lonely and in misery.

L.16: Turn to me and be gracious to me, for I [am] alone and afflicted.

R.16: Look at me and be kind to me. I am all alone, and I am suffering.

decisions.choice: turn to me: turn your face toward me
decisions.reason: To turn to someone is to give them attention and favor (Leviticus 26:9); the opposite of hiding the face (27:9).

decisions.choice: alone: lonely, without help
decisions.reason: The word (yachid) means only or single (Genesis 22:2); of a person in trouble, alone, with no one to help (68:7).

decisions.choice: afflicted: poor and oppressed
decisions.reason: The word ('ani) is the afflicted person who has no power to help himself (9:13).

records.source: צָר֣וֹת לְבָבִ֣י הִרְחִ֑יבוּ מִ֝מְּצֽוּקוֹתַ֗י הוֹצִיאֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: [The] distresses of my heart they have made wide; from my troubles bring me out.
pieces: The troubles in my heart have grown larger and larger; rescue me from the tight places I am in.

L.17: The distresses of my heart have grown wide; bring me out of my troubles.

R.17: My heart is full of more and more troubles. Get me out of the hard times I am going through.

decisions.choice: have grown wide: the troubles have increased
alternatives: relieve the troubles of my heart
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the distresses of my heart have made wide", that is, they have grown. If the last letter of the verb is read with the next word, the line becomes a prayer: "relieve the distresses of my heart, and bring me out of my troubles". The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: troubles: narrow places, distress
decisions.reason: The word (metsuqot) is from a root meaning to press or narrow. The picture is of being hemmed in; compare 4:2, where God "made room" for the psalmist.

decisions.choice: the tight places I am in
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of narrowness (m2).

records.source: רְאֵ֣ה עָ֭נְיִי וַעֲמָלִ֑י וְ֝שָׂ֗א לְכָל־חַטֹּאותָֽי׃
records.gloss: See my affliction and my trouble, and forgive all my sins.
pieces: See my misery and my toil, and lift the weight of all my sins from me.

L.18: See my affliction and my trouble, and take away all my sins.

R.18: See how much I am hurting and how hard my life is. Forgive me for all my sins.

decisions.choice: take away: lift and carry away, forgive
decisions.reason: The verb (nasa') means to lift or carry; of sins, to take them away, to forgive (Exodus 34:7; Psalm 32:5).

decisions.choice: trouble: toil, hardship
decisions.reason: The word ('amal) is hard labor and the misery that goes with it.

decisions.choice: See: the alphabet skips a letter
decisions.reason: This verse begins with the same letter (resh) as verse 19; the letter that should come before it (qof) has no verse.

records.source: רְאֵֽה־אוֹיְבַ֥י כִּי־רָ֑בּוּ וְשִׂנְאַ֖ת חָמָ֣ס שְׂנֵאֽוּנִי׃
records.gloss: See my enemies, for they have become many, and [with] hatred of violence they have hated me.
pieces: Look how my enemies have multiplied, and how violent is the hatred they hold against me.

L.19: See my enemies, how many they have become, and [with] violent hatred they have hated me.

R.19: See how many enemies I have! They hate me so much that they want to hurt me.

decisions.choice: violent hatred: hatred that does harm
decisions.reason: The word (chamas) is violence, wrong done by force (11:5). Their hatred does not stop at feeling.

decisions.choice: they want to hurt me
decisions.reason: Readable says what violent hatred means (m1).

records.source: שָׁמְרָ֣ה נַ֭פְשִׁי וְהַצִּילֵ֑נִי אַל־אֵ֝ב֗וֹשׁ כִּֽי־חָסִ֥יתִי בָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I have taken refuge in you.
pieces: Keep my life safe and set me free; do not let me be disgraced, for I have made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my refuge.

L.20: Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I have taken refuge in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.20: Keep me safe and rescue me. Do not let me end up ashamed, because I have run to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for safety.

decisions.choice: taken refuge: run to God for shelter
decisions.reason: As in 2:12 and 7:2, the verb (chasah) is to seek shelter; here it is the ground of the plea.

decisions.choice: be put to shame
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: let my trust not be shown up as foolish.

decisions.choice: my life
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) here is the person's life, which is in danger.

records.source: תֹּם־וָיֹ֥שֶׁר יִצְּר֑וּנִי כִּ֝֗י קִוִּיתִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Integrity and uprightness, may they preserve me, for I have waited for you.
pieces: May integrity and uprightness stand guard over me, for I wait for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.21: Integrity and uprightness — may they preserve me, for I have waited for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.21: Let honesty and goodness protect me, because I am waiting for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to help me.

decisions.choice: integrity and uprightness: pictured as guards
decisions.reason: The two qualities are pictured as guards, as loyal love and faithfulness are in 40:12 and 61:8. They may be the psalmist's own way of life, or God's goodness and uprightness (verse 8) keeping him.

decisions.choice: I have waited for you
decisions.reason: As in verses 3 and 5.

decisions.choice: to help me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the psalmist waits for.

records.source: פְּדֵ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִ֝כֹּ֗ל צָֽרוֹתָיו׃
records.gloss: Redeem, God, Israel from all its troubles.
pieces: God, set Israel free from all its troubles.

L.22: Redeem, God, Israel out of all its troubles.

R.22: God, rescue Israel from all its troubles.

decisions.choice: redeem: set free, as by paying a price
decisions.reason: The verb (padah) is to buy back or set free, as God freed Israel from slavery in Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: a closing prayer for the whole people
decisions.reason: This verse begins with the letter pe and stands outside the alphabet (see verse 1); it calls God "God" rather than "the LORD" and widens the prayer to all Israel. Psalm 34, another alphabet poem, also ends with a verse beginning with pe about redeeming (34:23).
